copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Spain v Cabo Verde in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Monday, and the model and the market disagree on the the draw side by +3.1pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Elo numbers going in: Spain 2010, Cabo Verde 1540. That's a 470-point lead for Spain — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Spain to win at 84%, the draw at 10%, and Cabo Verde to win at 6%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Spain to win at 90%, the draw at 7%, and Cabo Verde to win at 4%. Polymarket has the draw at 7%, which prices out at American odds of +1349; the model has the same side at 10%. The +3.1pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On the draw, that haircut lands the model at 10%; the market is at 7%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +3.1pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff 24 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +3.1pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Spain are a justifiably popular pick as the reigning European champions have plenty of world-class talent.

copy.summary: This is one of the few matches where the model leans toward the draw more than Polymarket does. The model rates the draw at 10%, the market at 7% — a +3.1pp gap.
copy.title: Spain v Cabo Verde · the model leans the draw
